One hundred prisoners. One hundred boxes. And one very strange deal.
100 prisoners · 100 boxes
Each prisoner's number is hidden inside one of the boxes, shuffled at random.
Each number hidden in a box
One at a time, each prisoner may open fifty boxes, looking for their own number.
Open up to 50 boxes
Then every box is closed again. No marks, no signals, no talking.
No signals. No talking.
If every single prisoner finds their number, they all go free. If even one fails, nobody does.
All 100 must find it
Guessing at random, their chance is about one in a million trillion trillion.
Random guessing ≈ 0%
Is there a better plan? Pause, and comment yours!
Comment your plan!
Here's the trick. First, open the box with your own number on the lid.
Open YOUR number's box first
Whatever number is inside, open that box next. And keep following the chain.
Follow the chain
The boxes always form loops, so the chain must lead back to your own number.
Every chain loops back to you
Let's try it with eight boxes, and four tries each.
Try it: 8 boxes, 4 tries
Prisoner three opens box three. Inside is six. Box six holds one. And box one holds three. Found it!
That loop has three boxes, so everyone on it finds their number in three tries.
Loop of 3 = 3 tries
The plan only fails if some loop is longer than half the boxes.
Fails only if a loop is too long
With a hundred boxes, there's no loop that long about thirty one percent of the time.
No long loop ≈ 31% of the time
So their chance jumps from almost zero, to thirty one percent!
